Here is what the approved guides say:

Phnom Penh in three days. Day one suits the riverfront: the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda open in the morning, then the National Museum, and sunset along Sisowath Quay. Day two covers the sobering sites: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum and the Choeung Ek memorial are best done together in a half day with a quiet afternoon afterward. Day three is for markets and food: Central Market in the morning and Russian Market for souvenirs, then a cooking class or street-food crawl. [1]

Planning your Angkor visit. Angkor passes are sold in one-day, three-day and seven-day versions at the official ticket centre, and prices change, so confirm the current price before travelling. The small circuit covers Angkor Wat, Bayon and Ta Prohm; the grand circuit adds Preah Khan and other temples. Sunrise at Angkor Wat is popular and crowded; consider starting at Ta Prohm early to avoid the crowds. Start before 8 am to avoid the midday heat and bring water. [2]

A relaxed Kampot weekend. Spend the first morning cycling to a pepper farm and salt fields, then settle by the river for lunch. In the afternoon take a sunset river cruise. The second day suits Bokor National Park, ideally starting early to beat the heat, and a visit to caves on the way back. Finish with seafood at the market. Kep is an easy half-day extension. [3]

sources.title: Southern coast transport
sources.snippet: Southern coast transport. 5 hours per leg depending on route and traffic. Schedules change; confirm times with your guesthouse or operator. Within Kampot and Kep, tuk-tuks and rented bicycles are common. Boats to Rabbit Island depart from Kep.
